claims.text: A nanometer-scale conformal Al2O3 layer can be inserted at the interface between an elemental Cr coating and a zirconium-alloy substrate by atomic layer deposition.
Grain boundaries in the standard Cr coating permit elevated-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
The inserted Al2O3 film will be dense and nanometer-thick.
The Al2O3 film will conformally adhere at the Cr/Zr interface.
The Al2O3 interlayer will remain intact and stable in subcritical water at temperatures up to 400°C.
The Al2O3 interlayer will remain intact and stable during steam exposure at 1000–1100°C for approximately 30 minutes.
Al2O3 has a high melting point, chemical inertness, and extremely low atomic diffusivity relevant to the proposed service conditions.
The Al2O3 layer will physically obstruct Cr and Zr migration across the coating–substrate interface.
Obstruction of Cr and Zr migration by the Al2O3 layer will significantly reduce interdiffusion during transient high-temperature exposure.
The Al2O3 interlayer will leave the protective oxidation properties of the outer Cr coating unaltered.
Relative to an unmodified Cr-coated baseline, the Al2O3-containing coating will exhibit markedly reduced Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
Relative to the baseline, the Al2O3-containing coating will exhibit delayed failure during 1000–1100°C steam transients lasting about 30 minutes.
The Al2O3-containing coating will maintain corrosion and oxidation protection during extended subcritical-water exposure at up to 400°C.
An unmodified elemental Cr coating on zirconium alloy undergoes accelerated high-temperature Cr–Zr interdiffusion that causes premature coating failure under accident conditions.
The proposed effectiveness boundary is subcritical water at no more than 400°C during routine operation.
The proposed accident-effectiveness boundary is steam at 1000–1100°C for approximately 30 minutes.
Long-term adhesion and mechanical integrity under repeated thermal cycling may limit the Al2O3 barrier's performance.
Nanoscale defects in the Al2O3 barrier may evolve during service and limit its effectiveness.

contradictions.description: The initial state describes Cr as already deposited directly on the zirconium-alloy substrate, while the intervention calls for depositing Al2O3 between the pre-deposited Cr coating and the substrate. An interfacial ALD layer would ordinarily need to be deposited before the Cr coating unless a distinct post-deposition insertion method is specified.
